cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is a "skill-enforced development workflow," and how does it differ from process guidance placed in a prompt?
cards.answer: A software process (spec, decompose into judgement-free tasks, implement test-first, review, land) encoded as a chain of agent skills that trigger automatically at phase boundaries — mandatory files the agent must consult when it reaches each phase, rather than prompt-based advice that a long session drifts away from.

cards.heading: Bootstrap mechanism
cards.question: What single standing rule does the session-start bootstrap instruction establish, and when is it re-injected?
cards.answer: Check for a relevant skill before starting any task; on harnesses that expose the hook, it is re-injected after context compaction too.

cards.heading: Planning skill granularity
cards.question: How granular are the tasks the planning skill produces, and who are they written for?
cards.answer: Tasks of a few minutes each, carrying exact file paths, complete code, and verification steps — written explicitly for "an enthusiastic junior engineer with no judgement and no project context," i.e. specified until execution requires no judgement at all.

cards.heading: Fresh subagent per task
cards.question: Why does implementation dispatch a fresh subagent per task with two-stage review, rather than one continuous session?
cards.answer: So working context never accumulates across tasks — the plan, not the transcript, carries continuity, enabling hours of unattended progress without transcript drift. The two review stages check spec compliance first, then code quality.

cards.heading: Test-first enforcement
cards.question: How is test-first development enforced in this workflow, as opposed to merely recommended?
cards.answer: Destructively: any code written before its failing test exists is deleted.

cards.heading: Portability across harnesses
cards.question: Why is this methodology portable across many different agent harnesses?
cards.answer: The whole process ships as a set of skill files rather than harness-specific code, so it installs into a dozen unrelated harnesses through each one's own plugin mechanism, and it is testable via a meta-skill for authoring skills plus an eval harness that exercises skill behaviour.
